source.title: TESSERA v2: Scaling Pixel-wise Earth Foundation Models
source.authors: Zheng-Peng Feng; S. Jaffer; Ira J. S. Shokar; J. Knezevic; James G. C. Ball; Pedro Sousa; M. Elvers; Madeline C. Lisaius; C. Atzberger; Robin Young; A. Naik; Nial H. Robinson; David A. Coomes; A. Madhavapeddy; Srinivasan Keshav

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. There is localized text corruption in part of Appendix I; the main scaling-study results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study extends scaling-law analysis to pixel-wise Earth-observation encoders and tests whether downstream performance relates to pretraining loss and generalizes with model scale. It does not test language-model cross-entropy laws.
record.gate_note: The paper reports downstream scores and BARLOW TWINS loss, not held-out language-model cross-entropy scaling. Its allocation fits optimize downstream score, not pretraining loss. Cited findings from other studies and unrelated benchmark comparisons are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests downstream predictability (V6) in a new setting: 395 pixel-wise Sentinel-1/2 Barlow Twins encoders on 15 Earth-observation tasks. It reports the loss–downstream correlation, and out-of-sample extrapolation of a downstream scaling fit to 0.5–2B teachers. It also shows that the fitted allocation exponent depends on the selection criterion (V7). It never fits held-out pretraining loss against parameters, data or compute, so V1, V2, V3 and V5 are not tested as stated.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. The authors conclude that Barlow Twins pretraining loss barely predicts downstream EO performance, so loss-based selection wastes about 2–5× compute and EO scaling laws should be fit to downstream metrics. The downstream-optimal allocation grows encoder and data while the projector stays fixed, and the resulting law extrapolates to 0.5–2B teachers. They restrict the laws to this architecture family, objective and task suite.
record.recipe_differences: This is an Earth-observation study using pixel-wise Sentinel-1/2 encoders and BARLOW TWINS loss. It fits allocation laws to downstream composite score and d-pixel data rather than to language-model held-out cross-entropy and text tokens.
record.method_sensitivity: The fitted encoder exponent differs with selection criterion: 0.36 for downstream-score-optimal peaks versus 0.02 for loss-optimal peaks. The data exponent is derived from the iso-FLOP constraint rather than fitted independently; projector fitting uses mid-to-high compute slices.

fits_no_version.finding: For the score-optimal allocation, encoder size ∝ C^0.36 and projector ∝ C^0.011 (indistinguishable from zero). The data exponent of 0.63 is derived from the iso-FLOP constraint rather than fitted. The split is data-heavy, departing from Hoffmann's balanced split.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In pixel-wise Sentinel-1/2 Barlow Twins encoders, the downstream-score-optimal encoder size grows as C^0.36, with data absorbing the rest; projector size stays fixed.

fits_no_version.finding: When the lowest Barlow Twins loss is chosen per bucket, the encoder size barely grows with compute (C^0.02). This is the loss-based allocation counterpart to V3 in a new modality, but it rests on an argmin over single runs with no CI.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In EO Barlow Twins pretraining, the loss-optimal encoder size is nearly compute-invariant, unlike language-model compute-optimal laws.

record.problems: The authors limit the fitted laws to one pixel-wise Sentinel-1/2 architecture family, one self-supervised objective, and one 15-task evaluation suite. The compute cost estimate for loss-based selection is based on nine bucket peaks and is described as sensitive to loss noise and winner’s-curse effects.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant row exceeded the 60-row limit. The paper’s other downstream benchmark results, distillation and embedding-prefix experiments, and cited results from earlier studies are outside the tested claim versions.

untested.parts: No power-law fit of held-out pretraining loss against parameters, data or compute.
Extrapolates downstream score, not pretraining loss.

The allocation law is fit to the downstream-score optimum. No loss-minimising allocation with uncertainty is fitted; only the bare C^0.02 loss-selected encoder exponent is given (see fits_no_version).
The architecture sweep (Table 3) varies structural axes and scores them on three downstream tasks. It does not hold parameter count fixed and does not report loss.
There is no loss power law in the EO modality. Only the allocation exponents follow power laws.
Language-model downstream tasks are not studied. Only one EO model family and one task suite are tested.
Parameter-counting conventions, schedules, data and fitting methods are not varied. Only the selection criterion (score vs loss) is compared.

missing.what: The score-optimal per-slice peak score rises log-linearly with compute, slope 0.0886 per compute decade. This is the downstream-vs-compute envelope.
A 44M encoder trained from scratch on the teacher's data budget scores 0.527. The authors say it sits on the per-encoder-best curve, which is extra evidence of downstream score vs scale.
Exponent stability: LOBO mean ±σ of 0.36±0.01 for the encoder and 0.63±0.01 for data, plus bootstrap CIs.

record.verdict_notes: V6 is treated as applying to this new setting (T3), since the version does not name language models. Under a strict system-kind reading, all V6 rows would become fits_no_version. The loss used is the normalised Barlow Twins validation loss, not cross-entropy. The authors themselves contrast EO with language and vision, where they say loss tracks downstream quality.

versions.untested_parts: Does not fit held-out pretraining loss as a power law in parameters, tokens, or compute.
Extrapolates downstream scores, not held-out pretraining loss, from smaller runs.
Fits a downstream-score-optimal allocation, not a loss-minimizing allocation; the data quantity is d-pixels, not training tokens.
Does not compare depth, width, or architecture at fixed parameter count to test their effect on loss.
Studies Earth-observation models, but does not test whether held-out pretraining loss follows the same power law in other modalities or training regimes.
Tests downstream scores for this EO model family and task suite only; it does not test language-model downstream tasks.
Compares loss-based and downstream-score-based model selection in this setup; it does not systematically vary parameter-counting conventions, schedules, data, or fitting methods.

rows.subject: TESSERA v2 395-run sweep
rows.operation_detail: Compared selecting the highest-downstream-score run with selecting the lowest-loss run in each compute bucket.
rows.measure: Additional compute required for loss-based selection to match downstream-score-based selection
rows.value: roughly 2–5× the compute; point estimate about 3.5×
rows.uncertainty: 95% interval for excess fraction [156%, 451%], corresponding to compute multiple about 2.6 to 5.5×
rows.note: The authors say the estimate is sensitive to loss noise and winner’s-curse effects.
rows.check: This is a derived quantity: the per-slice score gap (0.0486) divided by the envelope slope (0.0886). It is not a direct correlation. The authors say winner's-curse selection and loss noise inflate it. Keep it as a consequence of r1–r11, not as independent evidence.

conditions.value: Lowest normalized BARLOW TWINS loss per compute bucket

rows.note: The paper reports the loss-selected law as nearly flat and says the two laws diverge as compute grows.
rows.check: The loss-selected fit is an argmin over single runs per bucket. It has no reported CI and no LOBO, unlike the score-selected fit (CI [+0.31, +0.39], LOBO 0.36±0.01). The two fits differ in robustness, and the row should note this.

rows.subject: TESSERA v2 0.5B teacher
rows.stage_stated: Pretrained teacher; evaluated on the 15-task ALPHA EARTH suite
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated an out-of-sample teacher against the downstream-score scaling fit made on the smaller sweep.

conditions.value: Encoder law fit on sweep runs up to 278 M; teacher not used in fit

rows.note: The authors state that the teacher lands on the extrapolated curve.
rows.check: The paper gives no predicted values or residuals, only the statement that the teachers land on the curve. The teachers also differ from the sweep runs: wider dual-branch model, a 9-layer projector of about 170M, and a single epoch over about 14B d-pixels. The row should note that 'on the curve' is the authors' visual claim.

relationships.condition: Pretraining loss as predictor of downstream score, EO Barlow Twins sweep, pooled and within each of nine iso-FLOP buckets
relationships.reason: Pooled Pearson r = −0.18 and Spearman ρ = −0.16; within-bucket ρ ranges from −0.25 to +0.07, so loss does not rank runs (r1–r11). Loss-based selection costs about 2.6–5.5× compute (r12).
relationships.display_finding: Pooled correlations were Pearson r = −0.18 and Spearman ρ = −0.16; within nine groups matched for compute, ρ ranged from −0.25 to +0.07, and selecting models by loss cost about 2.6–5.5× as much compute.

source_check.reason: Section 3.2 and Appendix G report pooled r = −0.18 and ρ = −0.16, with within-bucket ρ from −0.25 to +0.07; the authors explicitly conclude that loss cannot reliably rank downstream performance.

relationships.condition: Downstream score vs encoder scale, with the score-based law extrapolated from runs of at most 278M to out-of-sample 0.5/1/2B teachers
relationships.reason: The teachers score 0.572, 0.596 and 0.608, improving monotonically, and the authors say they land on the extrapolated curve. No residuals are reported (r15–r17).
relationships.display_finding: Held-out 0.5B, 1B and 2B teachers scored 0.572, 0.596 and 0.608, respectively, and reportedly lay on the curve extrapolated from models up to 278M.

relationships.display_finding: The compute-optimal encoder exponent was 0.36 under score selection, with confidence interval [0.31, 0.39], versus 0.02 under loss selection.
